registration.note: MSA membership (compulsory to present) plus conference fee; Lund's own fee isn't published yet, so estimated from the prior Lima 2024 tiered schedule (PhD/low-income-country tier: EUR 45) plus an estimated membership fee

travel.note: HYD-Copenhagen/Malmo return, regional heuristic for India-Europe, booked 8-10 weeks ahead

visa.note: Schengen short-stay visa; official Sweden fee is EUR 80 plus a VFS service charge. Research students/researchers may qualify for a Schengen fee waiver - worth checking before assuming the full fee applies.

fit.reason: Her secondary topic 'Partition memory online' (weight 0.55) and her broader interest in platform-based counterpublics fit the 'memory, responsibility, hope' theme, but her top-weighted topics (caste & digital media, Dalit & Bahujan counterpublics) aren't a named track here, making this plausible-with-framing rather than a core home.

standing.reason: Hosted by a learned society (Memory Studies Association) with confirmed, recognizable keynotes (Pumla Gobodo-Madikizela, Emilie Pine, Oksana Zabuzhko); the number of past editions and indexing status aren't stated in the extraction.

network.reason: MSA's flagship annual conference offers broad international networking in memory studies, though none of the confirmed keynotes overlap with her specific citation neighborhood (Udupa, Arora, Gillespie, etc.).

outcomes.reason: No proceedings, special issue, or paper award is mentioned for the main conference; the structured feedback format for postgraduates is bundled into the separate MSA Forward preconference workshop instead.

feasibility.reason: Only the high end of the cost estimate (~Rs1.65L) exceeds her Rs1.5L budget; a Schengen visa is a moderate (not severe) hurdle against her 'prefer_none' visa tolerance; partial credit given since MSA travel grants/waivers and the ICSSR scheme could cover a meaningful share, though amounts aren't yet confirmed.

fit.rationale: MSA Lund's theme, 'memory, responsibility, hope', is a natural home for her secondary interest in Partition memory online, and her broader work on how platforms shape collective counterpublic narratives has a real conceptual link to memory studies.
